title: Week 36 Mastery Quiz · Senior Thesis, Oral Defense, and Cumulative Final

questions.question: A thesis defense cites ICJ Statute Article 36 as proof the Court may hear any dispute. What should an examiner ask?
options: Which jurisdictional basis and conditions permit the particular case to proceed?
Whether the Court's building is accessible.
Whether the applicant's claim is popular.
Which party supplied more pages.
questions.explanation: Which jurisdictional basis and conditions permit the particular case to proceed?

questions.question: A graduation portfolio contains all lessons but one weekly mastery quiz at 70%. Which claim follows the Academy's existing mastery policy?
options: An 80% course average overrides the weak quiz.
The week still requires an 80% or higher best quiz result before its gate is met.
The senior thesis erases every weekly requirement.
Quiz attempts cannot be repeated.
questions.explanation: The week still requires an 80% or higher best quiz result before its gate is met.

questions.question: A senior reports the thesis achieved 85% but the oral defense was not evaluated. What remains unresolved?
options: All final requirements are automatically met.
The evaluator's signature is optional in every case.
The separately required defense evaluation and any other credit gates.
The thesis grade proves the defense score.
questions.explanation: The separately required defense evaluation and any other credit gates.

questions.question: A presentation chart combines noncomparable historical years. What response demonstrates command of limitations?
options: Claim the audience cannot notice.
Choose only years favorable to the thesis.
Replace the chart with a slogan.
Acknowledge the mismatch, correct or bound the comparison and explain possible effects.
questions.explanation: Acknowledge the mismatch, correct or bound the comparison and explain possible effects.

questions.question: The final oral examiner introduces a verified primary source inconsistent with the conclusion. What demonstrates academic integrity?
options: Assess the document's relevance and revise or qualify the thesis where warranted.
Dismiss it because the draft is complete.
Change the document's date.
Attack the examiner rather than address evidence.
questions.explanation: Assess the document's relevance and revise or qualify the thesis where warranted.

questions.question: A final thesis contains a source link that no longer resolves. What is the strongest preservation response?
options: Leave an unexplained broken link.
Supply a stable archival citation, document metadata and a verifiable alternative source location.
Replace it with an unrelated homepage.
Delete the claim's evidence record.
questions.explanation: Supply a stable archival citation, document metadata and a verifiable alternative source location.

questions.question: A senior claims a correlation constitutes independent proof of policy causation. How should the defense improve?
options: Repeat the correlation more emphatically.
Discard all contrary cases.
Discuss confounders, mechanism, temporal order and counterfactual limits before claiming causality.
State that uncertainty is disallowed.
questions.explanation: Discuss confounders, mechanism, temporal order and counterfactual limits before claiming causality.

questions.question: A student reuses an earlier assignment without disclosing the duplication in the capstone. What should the evaluator require?
options: Assume self-reuse never matters.
Count the same text as two independent findings.
Remove all prior records.
Clear attribution and disclosure of reused work consistent with academic integrity rules.
questions.explanation: Clear attribution and disclosure of reused work consistent with academic integrity rules.

questions.question: A fictional capstone makes claims about real identifiable interviewees without consent. What is the proper final-review concern?
options: Ethical collection, participant protection, lawful use and whether claims are adequately supported.
Only the word count.
Whether the interviewees share a political position.
Whether private names make the thesis persuasive.
questions.explanation: Ethical collection, participant protection, lawful use and whether claims are adequately supported.

questions.question: A final graduation screen shows passing grades but missing evaluator approval. What should the system do?
options: Issue credit because the user clicked a button.
Keep credit locked until the established evaluator and graduation requirements are satisfied.
Use only the average weekly grade.
Remove approval requirements at graduation.
questions.explanation: Keep credit locked until the established evaluator and graduation requirements are satisfied.

shortResponse: Can the student independently defend a rigorous conclusion, acknowledge limits, apply four years of social studies, and satisfy every graduation gate?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
